title: Three teams see ultracold fermion gases turn more transparent

items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2103.06921: Pauli blocking of light scattering in degenerate fermions
passages: Pauli blocking also occurs when free atoms scatter light elastically (Rayleigh scattering) and the final external momentum states are already occupied.
Higher electronic orbitals cannot decay to lower-lying states if they are already occupied -- this is Pauli blocking due to occupation of internal states.
Pauli blocking of spontaneous emission is responsible for the stability of atoms.
Here we report the creation of a dense Fermi gas of ultracold lithium atoms and show that at low temperatures light scattering is suppressed.
We also explore the suppression of inelastic light scattering when two colliding atoms emit light shifted in frequency.
A suppression of the total rate of light scattering requires a quantum-degenerate Fermi gas with a Fermi energy larger than the photon recoil energy.

crossref.title: Observation of Pauli blocking in light scattering from quantum degenerate fermions
crossref.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2103.02319: Observation of Pauli blocking in light scattering from quantum degenerate fermions
passages: Deb, Niels Kjærgaard View a PDF of the paper titled Observation of Pauli blocking in light scattering from quantum degenerate fermions, by Amita B.

We attribute the observed increased transmission of light through the quantum degenerate Fermi gas to Pauli blocking, where Fermi-Dirac statistics causes atoms to occupy a large region of the momentum space limiting the number of accessible states for the scattered atom.
The Pauli exclusion principle forbids indistinguishable fermions to occupy the same quantum mechanical state.
Here we perform measurements on the scattering of off-resonant light from ultracold gasses of fermionic atoms.
For Fermi gases in the quantum degenerate regime, we observe a marked suppression in light scattering as compared to a similarly prepared thermal Bose gas.

Our work confirms a longstanding fundamental result in the theory of the optical response of quantum gases and is an important step towards novel cooling and thermometry mechanisms for degenerate Fermi gases.

items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2103.02216: Pauli blocking of atomic spontaneous decay
passages: Spontaneous decay of an excited atomic state is a fundamental process that originates from the interaction between matter and vacuum modes of the electromagnetic field.
The rate of decay can thus be engineered by modifying the density of final states of the joint atom-photon system.
Imposing suitable boundary conditions on the electromagnetic field has been shown to alter the density of vacuum modes near the atomic transition, resulting in modified atomic decay rates.

Here we report the first experimental demonstration of suppression of atomic radiative decay by reducing the density of available energy-momentum modes of the atomic motion when it is embedded inside a Fermi sea.
